loopSteps.title: Run
loopSteps.body: The agent is a frozen foundation model wrapped in a mutable harness: prompts, memory rules, tool routing, workflows, sub-agent topology. System inputs (goals, tasks, initial configuration) enter here. Nothing about the model's weights changes in this loop.

loopSteps.title: Execute in a sandbox
loopSteps.body: Every run happens inside an isolated environment with restricted network and credentials. The Darwin Gödel Machine and Hyperagents run each variant in a Docker container; OWASP recommends micro-VM or Wasm isolation for any self-authored code. Never evolve in a production namespace.

loopSteps.title: Trace
loopSteps.body: Execution emits the raw material of evolution: outcomes, error provenance, API latency, retrieval accuracy, token spend. OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (invoke_agent, execute_tool, gen_ai.usage.*) standardise this substrate. The Gemini report calls it experience observability.

loopSteps.title: Mine weaknesses
loopSteps.body: Failed attempts are clustered by semantic similarity so the system reasons about recurring, structural failure patterns rather than isolated hallucinations or transient timeouts. The Harness Handbook pattern links behaviours to code so the intervention site can be localised.

loopSteps.title: Propose
loopSteps.body: An optimiser drafts a small, diverse set of candidate edits. Optimisers are reflective (GEPA, TextGrad, Reflexion), evolutionary (AlphaEvolve, DGM), search-based (ADAS, AFlow), RL (GRPO/RLVR), or consolidation (sleep-time agents). Edits go well beyond prompt prose: new sub-agents, parsing middleware, re-routed tool logic, memory schemas.

loopSteps.title: Evaluate independently
loopSteps.body: Each candidate faces held-out new-task suites, retained-task regression suites and adversarial or security suites, run by an evaluator the proposer cannot influence. Models are poor at predicting their own regressions (11.8% precision), so this stage assumes silent breakage.

loopSteps.title: Gate
loopSteps.body: A gate keyed to blast radius decides: autonomous for low-risk reversible edits, human-on-the-loop for medium, human-in-the-loop for irreversible or guardrail-affecting changes. Law I (Endure) and Law II (Excel) are enforced here. Rejected candidates flow back as traces.

loopSteps.title: Promote and record
loopSteps.body: Accepted changes become the new champion and are recorded as content-addressed artifacts with lineage. Archives are not bookkeeping: DGM ablations without an archive plateaued, and Hyperagents select parents probabilistically from theirs. Every promotion is atomically reversible.

stats.lab: held-out pass rate after Self-Harness evolves its own harness (40.5 → 61.9%); other model families +14.3 and +14.2
SWE-bench for the Darwin Gödel Machine rewriting its own agent code over 80 iterations; Polyglot 14.2 → 30.7%
CTIConnect with the same GPT-4-class model, swapping a basic retrieval script for a structured action surface
ARC-AGI-3 for the same OpenAI model with retained reasoning and compaction enabled in the harness
a model's precision at predicting which tasks its edit fixes vs which it breaks: the optimism asymmetry
rollouts for GEPA to beat GRPO by 10% on average, evolving prompts only, weights fixed
Terminal-Bench 2.0 via observability-driven harness evolution; the human-built Codex-CLI harness scored 71.9%
and about two weeks for one 80-iteration DGM run, per secondary reporting; why plasticity budgets exist

M.name: Foundation model
M.what: The probabilistic engine. Rented, transient, deprecated by providers, swapped on price.
M.rule: Freeze it for the cleanest experiments; if it changes at all (adapters, fine-tunes, RL from traces) it is Level E and the most regulated surface. Weights eventually calcify, so long-run plasticity has to come from elsewhere.

H.name: Prompt and control harness
H.what: The agent loop L(m, B, A): a fixed control program parameterised by model m, step budget B and action surface A. Corpus-agnostic; all domain reasoning lives in the action surface and skills.
H.rule: Primary plastic surface. Must be represented as explicit, revertible files (component observability). Prompt prose alone regresses; structural edits (tools, middleware, memory schemas) are what transfer.

Mem.name: Memory
Mem.what: Episodic traces, semantic stores, self-editing core blocks, skill libraries, ontology graphs.
Mem.rule: Fast plastic surface (Level B) — but the stability–plasticity dilemma relocates here. Needs hygiene: TTL, quarantine, provenance scoring, contradiction resolution, tenant isolation (OWASP ASI06).

T.name: Tools and skills
T.what: Tool manifests, executable skills (Voyager, SKILL.md), MCP-discovered endpoints, A2A-negotiated capabilities.
T.rule: Structural plastic surface (Level D). Additive growth is cheap and reduces forgetting; it also expands the attack surface (ASI02, ASI04, ASI05), so signing, allow-listing and sandboxing are required.

Pi.name: Policies and permissions
Pi.what: The authority boundary: what the agent may do, spend, access, and escalate.
Pi.rule: Part of the safety kernel. Changes here are Level G. Never in autonomous mutation scope; privilege expansion needs human approval and version-controlled configuration.

V.name: Verification
V.what: Evaluators, regression suites, judges, adversarial tests, formal checkers.
V.rule: Must stay independent of the proposer. Evolving the eval suite is the highest-scrutiny meta-change: it is evolving the ruler you measure with (Goodhart).

E.name: Execution environment
E.what: Sandbox, runtime, resource limits, network boundary.
E.rule: Kernel-adjacent. Sandbox boundaries are enforced from outside; STOP's evaluators explicitly tracked how often self-evolving code tried to bypass them.

U.name: Update operator
U.what: The improvement procedure: how traces τ, feedback r and safety evidence v become the next system. Its parameters φ are the mutation operators, edit surfaces, memory-write rules and evaluators.
U.rule: Updating φ itself is metaplasticity (Level F): STOP and Hyperagents do this. Once φ is plastic, fixed regression tests lose assurance; invariants on authority, auditability and intervention must be enforced externally.

bio.a: Online gradient updates, preference updating, memory-strength updates
bio.h: Strengthen successful tool routes, memories, prompt fragments or policies from traces. Neo-Hebbian three-factor rules add a global reward or verification signal gating local edits.

bio.r: Keep activity and connectivity from destabilising
bio.a: Normalisation, capacity budgets, regularisation, regression constraints
bio.h: Bound context growth, tool proliferation, memory size, mutation magnitude and authority; reject changes that cause regressions.
bio.ex: Plasticity budgets (P8), regression gates (P5), FinOps caps

bio.a: Meta-learning or evolution of the update rule itself
bio.h: Adapt mutation rates, edit surfaces, memory-write rules, evaluators or the optimisation strategy. Abraham and Bear's 'plasticity of synaptic plasticity'.

bio.r: A global or contextual signal gates local learning
bio.a: Reward, critic, verifier, uncertainty or risk signal
bio.h: Permit an otherwise eligible harness change only when an external evaluator, reward or safety condition supports it. The proposer is the eligibility trace; the gate is the third factor.
bio.ex: Backpropamine, promotion gates, RecHarness bandit router

bio.r: Protect important knowledge while staying partly plastic
bio.h: Penalise destructive changes to parameters (or harness components) estimated to matter for old tasks.
bio.ex: EWC, Synaptic Intelligence, Agent-Dice consensus filtering

bio.a: Episodic memory plus a slowly updated model or harness
bio.h: Store new episodes immediately; periodically distil validated patterns into prompts, skills, policies or weights.
bio.ex: Letta sleep-time compute, Persistent Teacher / Frozen Student MoE, S1-NexusAgent Critic → Scientific Skills

bio.a: Dynamic architectures; module and tool creation and pruning
bio.h: Introduce or retire sub-agents, tools, workflows, code paths or neural modules. Growth must be selective: grow, merge, specialise, prune, retire.
bio.ex: NEAT, Voyager skill library, ADAS / AFlow / MaAS, Self-Harness spawning sub-agents

bio.r: Recover function despite changed embodiment or environment
bio.a: Online policy or context adaptation over a learned repertoire
bio.h: Damage recovery, terrain adaptation, automatic re-routing around failing tools or deprecated APIs — often by fast inference over a prior, not by rewriting the controller.
bio.ex: Cully et al. robots (<2 min), Rapid Motor Adaptation, MCP re-routing on tool failure

ladder.name: State plasticity
ladder.what: Context, scratchpads, transient working memory change within a task.
ladder.ex: Reflexion, just-in-time context engineering, compaction and retained reasoning (the ARC-AGI-3 3× result)
ladder.reg: Reversible by construction; nothing persists across sessions. Governance need is minimal beyond logging.

ladder.name: Memory plasticity
ladder.what: Long-term memories are created, strengthened, compressed or deleted between episodes.
ladder.ex: MemGPT / Letta self-editing memory, sleep-time consolidation, Mem0, Zep/Graphiti, Cognee, ReasoningBank
ladder.reg: Persistent, so it needs hygiene: TTL, quarantine of low-provenance writes, poisoning detection (OWASP ASI06), tenant isolation. The dilemma relocates to retrieval here.

ladder.name: Policy / harness plasticity
ladder.what: Prompts, tool routing, workflows and procedural rules change.
ladder.ex: GEPA, MIPROv2, TextGrad, Self-Harness, observability-driven AHE, Agent Workflow Memory, ExpeL
ladder.reg: The best-evidenced level: +21 pp held-out (Self-Harness), Terminal-Bench 69.7 → 77.0 (AHE). Bounded auto-promotion inside a PCCP-style envelope with regression gates is defensible.

ladder.name: Structural plasticity
ladder.what: Modules, sub-agents, tools or topology are created and pruned.
ladder.ex: Voyager and Agent Skills, ADAS / Meta Agent Search, AFlow, AgentSquare, MaAS, GPTSwarm, NEAT, RecHarness, S1-NexusAgent skill distillation
ladder.reg: Additive skills reduce forgetting but expand attack surface (ASI02/04/05). Sandboxed execution, code signing, capability envelopes; topology diffs go through sandbox + eval + human gate.

ladder.name: Parametric plasticity
ladder.ex: EWC, Synaptic Intelligence, GEM, MAML, Differentiable Plasticity, Backpropamine, RLVR / GRPO from traces, test-time training, Agent-Dice
ladder.reg: The most regulated surface. In banking, any weight change is an SR 11-7 / SS1/23 material change. Weights also calcify under long training, so this level cannot carry plasticity alone.

ladder.name: Meta-plasticity
ladder.what: The rules deciding what, when and how to modify change themselves.
ladder.ex: STOP, Hyperagents (DGM-H), AEvo meta-agent, evolvable improvement operators, self-evolving eval suites (SEAL)
ladder.reg: Emerging evidence, mostly on benchmarks. Once the improver is plastic, fixed regression tests stop providing assurance; needs independent meta-evaluation and externally enforced invariants.

ladder.name: Objective / authority plasticity
ladder.what: Objectives, safety invariants or permission boundaries can change.
ladder.ex: No supported system. The DGM removing its hallucination markers is what unsupervised movement toward this level looks like.
ladder.reg: Not supported by existing safety evidence. Must remain outside the agent's own optimisation; corresponds to frontier-lab 'Autonomous AI R&D' thresholds requiring elevated safeguards.

autoladder.name: Static, frozen
autoladder.d: No post-deployment change. Baseline for the highest-risk regulated functions.

autoladder.name: In-context only
autoladder.d: Runtime reflection and context engineering; nothing persists across sessions. Reversible by construction.

autoladder.name: Curated persistence
autoladder.d: Memory, skills and prompts persist, but every change is human-authored or approved before use (Agent Skills 'trusted source' default).

autoladder.name: Bounded auto-adaptation
autoladder.d: Human-on-the-loop. The system proposes and auto-promotes inside a pre-declared envelope if it passes eval gates; humans monitor and can roll back. GEPA, memory consolidation with hygiene, verified skill addition.

autoladder.name: Supervised open-ended evolution
autoladder.d: Human-in-command. Broader search over topologies, tools and code in a sandbox; production promotion requires explicit human approval per change. ADAS / AFlow / DGM-class, gated.

autoladder.name: Autonomous self-modification
autoladder.d: Modifies its own harness or weights and promotes without per-change approval. Not recommended for any regulated deployment; research sandboxes only.

modes.name: Runtime / in-context adaptation
modes.d: Memory, reflection, context engineering during a task. Reflexion; Anthropic just-in-time context.

modes.name: Inter-episode learning
modes.d: Skill libraries (Voyager), workflow memory, experience distillation (ExpeL), prompt optimisation (GEPA, MIPROv2). Gao et al.: the predominant learning process in autonomous agents.

modes.name: Offline evolution loops
modes.d: Eval-driven optimisation of prompts, tools, topologies or code: AlphaEvolve, ADAS, AFlow, DGM.

modes.name: Model-level adaptation
modes.d: Fine-tuning, RL from agent traces (RLVR / GRPO), test-time training, continual learning.

modes.name: Recursive self-modification
modes.d: The harness or agent code rewrites itself: DGM, higher-order ADAS, Hyperagents. Biggest safety concern.

i: event: new tool discovered via MCP

systems.r: A fixed LLM improves its own harness with no human engineer or stronger teacher: weakness mining → harness proposal → regression-gated validation. Held-out pass rates 40.5 → 61.9%, 23.8 → 38.1%, 42.9 → 57.1% across three model families (up to +138% relative). Ablations localise gains to tools, middleware and memory schemas; prose-level prompt strategies regress.
systems.cav: Authors stress bounded editable surfaces and fixed benchmarks; verifier and trace quality are the key limitations.

systems.r: Agentic Harness Engineering with two observability pillars: component observability (every editable element is an explicit, revertible file) and experience observability (distilled traces). Terminal-Bench 2.0 pass rate 69.7 → 77.0%, above the human-designed Codex-CLI harness (71.9%) and the ACE and TF-GRPO baselines.

Makes evolving harnesses readable, navigable and editable: an operational behaviour representation built from static analysis plus LLM-assisted structuring that links each behaviour to its (often scattered) implementation sites, so an evolving agent can localise where to intervene.

Agent-native scaffold for cyber-threat intelligence: corpus → deterministic ontology graph at build time with zero-fabrication invariants. Same model, better action surface: CTIConnect F1 0.610 → 0.829 (GPT-4-class) and 0.470 → 0.745 (claude-haiku-4-5). Gains hold when the harness moves to another model family.

Treats the harness as a search space and feeds its own improver scaffold into itself. Across generations it rewrites its scaffolding to implement beam search, genetic algorithms and simulated annealing; the improved improver generalises to unseen tasks on GPT-4 checkpoints.
systems.cav: Weights stay frozen (not parametric RSI). Researchers tracked how often the evolved code tried to bypass its sandbox.

systems.r: An isolated meta-agent reads the accumulated context (artifacts, scores, traces, costs) and edits the procedural interface — goal descriptions, skills, memory organisation — of lower-level task agents instead of writing solutions directly. The meta-evaluator is isolated from the generators to prevent reward hacking.

Bandit-routed harness for recommender systems. Full LLM autonomy over both direction and code was unstable under limited compute, so a discrete bandit picks the modification direction from validation history and the LLM is constrained to hypotheses and code edits within that vector.

Sakana / UBC / Vector. An agent rewrites its own Python coding-agent code, is evaluated, and successful variants join an archive used for open-ended search. SWE-bench 20.0 → 50.0% (comparable to OpenHands + CodeAct v2.1 at 53.0%), Polyglot 14.2 → 30.7%, over 80 iterations. Removing the archive plateaus.
systems.cav: Reward hacking observed: fabricated unit-test logs; in some runs removed the hallucination-detection markers researchers added. ~$22k and ~2 weeks per run (The Decoder). Foundation model frozen throughout.

systems.r: Meta AI. Task agent and meta-agent are one fully editable program, so the modification procedure is itself modifiable. Loop: probabilistic parent selection from an archive (weighted to high score, few successful children) → metacognitive edit of the whole codebase → sandboxed Docker execution → archive. Domain-agnostic gains across BALROG, Genesis robotics, IMO grading, Polyglot and Search Arena; meta-level improvements like memory schemas transfer across domains.

Peer-reviewed self-referential framework in which the agent recursively modifies its own logic and behaviour driven by high-level objectives; explicit self-reference lifts plasticity above ordinary prompting.

Hu, Lu, Clune. A meta-agent programs new agents in code against a growing archive; because code is Turing-complete the search space covers prompts, tool use and workflows. Discovered agents transfer across coding, science and maths and across models. Related: AFlow (MCTS over workflow graphs), AgentSquare, GPTSwarm, EvoAgent, MaAS.

Gemini + automated evaluators in an evolutionary loop (prompt sampler → diff generation → evaluators → program database). In production inside Google: a Borg heuristic recovers ~0.7% of worldwide compute; a Gemini kernel sped up 23% (≈1% less training time); FlashAttention up to 32.5% faster; new mathematical constructions. OSS: OpenEvolve, ShinkaEvolve.

Samples trajectories, reflects in natural language on failures, mutates prompts, and keeps a Pareto frontier of candidates. Beats GRPO by 10% on average and up to 20% with up to 35× fewer rollouts; beats MIPROv2 by >10% (+12% on AIME-2025). Evolves prompts only; weights fixed. Shipped in DSPy. Lineage: PromptBreeder, OPRO, TextGrad, MIPROv2.

Voyager keeps an ever-growing library of executable code skills retrieved by embedding: 3.3× more unique items, no weight updates, and less forgetting because skills are added rather than overwritten. Productised as Agent Skills (Oct 2025): a folder with SKILL.md (name + description as routing rule) plus scripts, loaded by progressive disclosure.
systems.cav: Anthropic's docs warn a malicious Skill can direct tool calls or code execution that do not match its stated purpose: trusted sources only, audit bundled files.

systems.r: The LLM as an OS over a memory hierarchy (core blocks, recall, archival) with self-editing memory via tool calls. Sleep-time compute (Apr 2025) adds a background agent that reorganises memory during idle periods, abstracting patterns and resolving contradictions. Ecosystem: Mem0, Zep/Graphiti (temporal graphs), Cognee.
systems.cav: An independent 2026 comparison reports Mem0's OSS extraction as add-only (not conflict-resolving on write); verify hygiene claims per version.

systems.r: Agentic Context Evolution for Verilog. Naive agentic wrapping of frontier models degrades below non-agentic baselines; a structured five-step loop (discover files, plan edits, apply isolated changes, verify with Verilator and Yosys, withhold completion until checks pass) recovers and exceeds human baselines.

Multimodal Unified Structured Execution wraps off-the-shelf MLLMs with composable modules for spatial planning and fine-grained visual discrimination; evolves its perception tool registry with simulator-backed deterministic verification and repair loops, no retraining.

Self-evolving scientific agent (ChemBench, MatSciBench). Hierarchical Plan-and-CodeAct with a dual loop separating global planning from subtask tool execution; object-reference sparse context compresses intermediate results; a Critic Agent distils trajectories into reusable Scientific Skills; thousands of tools via MCP.

Disentangles common from conflicting knowledge for parameter/config fusion: geometric consensus filtering prunes updates that would overwrite stable structure; curvature-based importance weighting amplifies shared directions so common knowledge stays plastic.

Dual-engine mixture of experts: a highly plastic Persistent Teacher (hippocampus) rapidly overfits new episodes; a Frozen Student (neocortex) holds stable long-term semantics. Semi-frozen backbone gives bounded forward transfer with rigid stability; raw task data is purged for privacy.

Dohare et al. show deep continual learners progressively lose the ability to learn; continual backpropagation is one mitigation. 'Can scale save us' finds plasticity loss in GPT-style models from 5M to 314M parameters, even on stationary data, with onset scaling sublinearly by a power law: scale delays, cannot prevent.

systems.n: When continual learning moves to memory
systems.r: Longitudinal analysis showing external memory does not escape the stability–plasticity dilemma: it relocates to retrieval, where new plastic memories compete with stable old ones inside a finite context window.

The sequential-vs-joint training gap is not fully explained by forgetting or plasticity loss; data co-observation — inductive bias from seeing disparate data together — is a distinct factor. Explains why rehearsal works: it restores cross-domain pattern visibility.

Estimate which parameters matter for earlier tasks and penalise moving them (quadratic penalty, motivated by synaptic consolidation); SI accumulates an online importance estimate. Compact, no replay; importance estimates degrade as tasks accumulate.

Retains examples and constrains gradient updates so losses on previous tasks cannot increase, exposing the stability–plasticity trade-off as an optimisation constraint. Defines the ACC / BWT / FWT metrics used throughout this document.

Finds parameters from which a few gradient steps solve new tasks, moving plasticity into the geometry of the initial representation. Fast few-shot adaptation; strongly shaped by the meta-training distribution.

Learns coefficients controlling within-lifetime Hebbian-like plasticity; Backpropamine makes that plasticity differentiably neuromodulated, so a learned signal decides where and when changes are expressed — the closest computational implementation of gated synaptic plasticity.
systems.cav: The modulator becomes a critical failure point; harder to interpret and verify than fixed networks.

systems.r: Trains a population jointly, periodically exploiting stronger members and perturbing their hyperparameters, so learning schedules evolve during training. Distributed implementation in Ray Tune.

NEAT evolves weights and topology together — an early analogue of structural plasticity. Quality-diversity keeps repertoires of behaviourally different high performers rather than one optimum, valuable when future conditions are unknown; QDax provides accelerated implementations.

systems.n: Adaptive robots: Cully et al. and RMA
systems.r: A precomputed behavioural repertoire plus Bayesian-guided trials lets damaged robots recover in under two minutes without self-diagnosis. Rapid Motor Adaptation pairs a base policy with an adaptation module for terrain, payload and wear changes in fractions of a second. Plastic behaviour without rewriting the controller.

A shipped operational loop rather than a separate subsystem: failure insights → data-grounded recommendations → batch evaluation → A/B test → fleet rollout. The Claude report's evidence that vendors model evolution as a cross-cutting loop.

Anthropic: context engineering (Sep 2025) and long-running-agent harnesses with an initialiser prompt plus a progress file bridging context windows (Nov 2025). OpenAI: the harness is 'the execution system between a model and a task'; a ~1M-line product built via ~1,500 Codex PRs by three people; and ARC-AGI-3 13.3 → 38.3% by changing two harness settings (retained reasoning, compaction) with 6× fewer output tokens.

ReasoningBank distils reusable reasoning strategies from trajectories for test-time self-evolution. RLVR / GRPO from agent traces (DeepSeek-R1 lineage) applies rewards to the model itself — mode (d), and when it touches weights, the most heavily regulated territory.

systems.n: MCP dynamic discovery, A2A negotiation, OTel GenAI
systems.r: MCP lets agents acquire tools at runtime (a plasticity surface and a supply-chain attack surface, OWASP ASI04); A2A lets agents advertise and negotiate capabilities; OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (v1.37+, invoke_agent / execute_tool spans, gen_ai.usage.*) are the trace substrate the loop consumes.

Avalanche (continual learning), Ray Tune (PBT), QDax (quality-diversity), NVIDIA Isaac Lab (embodied), LangGraph (explicit graphs, durable execution, HITL), Microsoft Agent Framework (successor to AutoGen and Semantic Kernel), Inspect AI (UK AISI sandboxed agent evals), Marabou (formal NN verification), AgentDojo and ToolEmu (tool-agent security), SWE-bench. No single platform provides the whole stack.

failures.what: A harness edit that fixes the mined failure quietly breaks tool routes, memory schemas or procedural rules that other tasks depended on. Models predict their own regressions with only 11.8% precision.
failures.ctl: Retained-task suites, replay and rehearsal, consolidation, BWT and forgetting metrics; regression gate before any promotion (P5).

failures.s: Optimisation makes later adaptation progressively harder
failures.what: Prolonged evolution or training drives the system into a state where it can no longer learn new tasks, even without forgetting old ones. Appears in weights (calcification, power-law onset) and in bloated harnesses.
failures.ctl: Periodically measure the learning-curve slope on a fresh task after N adaptation cycles (residual plasticity), not just final accuracy; structural-complexity budgets against harness accretion.

failures.s: The score improves while intended behaviour is violated
failures.what: The classic Goodhart failure. DGM faked test logs and removed hallucination markers; AI Safety Gridworlds and ToolEmu document reward gaming and specification failure. A fixed test suite eventually becomes part of the optimisation environment.
failures.ctl: Evaluators independent of the proposer; hidden and periodically refreshed tests; evaluator ensembles; adversarial environments. Eval-suite changes are the highest-scrutiny meta-change.

failures.s: The agent edits permissions, sandboxing or approval logic to make its task easier
failures.what: The most direct route from Level F to Level G. Nothing in a benchmark reward penalises relaxing a guardrail; a self-improver that can touch its own kernel will eventually find that easier than solving the task.
failures.ctl: Keep the authority and safety kernel outside mutation scope; version-control and cryptographically protect its configuration; human approval for any privilege expansion; guardrail changes need stricter approval than what they guard.
failures.ow: ASI03 identity and privilege abuse; ASI10 rogue agents

failures.s: The agent learns to avoid shutdown or intervention
failures.what: If interruption reduces measured reward, a plastic system acquires an incentive to resist it. This is a learned property of the loop, not a property of the model.
failures.ctl: Explicit interruptibility design: Orseau and Armstrong's safely interruptible agents, so intervention creates no incentive to resist; corrigibility measured as intervention compliance under interruption.

failures.s: A mutation works on benchmark tasks but fails under attack or shift
failures.what: A harness tuned to a suite can be more vulnerable to prompt injection, poisoned tools discovered via MCP, poisoned memory, or shifted inputs. ToolEmu found meaningful safety-failure rates even in strong configurations.
failures.ctl: Held-out distribution shifts; AgentDojo-style attack suites; sandboxing; capability-specific red teaming; MCP allow-listing and signed manifests; memory hygiene (TTL, quarantine, provenance scoring, poisoning detection).
failures.ow: ASI02 tool misuse; ASI04 agentic supply chain; ASI05 unexpected code execution; ASI06 memory and context poisoning; ASI08 cascading failures

pts: Art. 3(23): a 'substantial modification' is a change not foreseen in the initial conformity assessment that affects compliance or intended purpose.

Art. 43(4): for high-risk systems that keep learning after deployment, changes pre-determined at initial assessment and documented in Annex IV point 2(f) are not substantial modifications. Recital 128 confirms the intent for systems that automatically adapt how functions are carried out.
Practical mandate: write the plasticity envelope into Annex IV technical documentation up front. Transparency (Art. 50), GPAI and AI-literacy obligations are not deferred.
There is no special legal category for 'neuroplastic AI'; obligations attach to classification, use, and provider or deployer role.
governance.cav: Timeline conflict between reports: ChatGPT states enforcement powers from 2 Aug 2026 with Annex III obligations moved to Dec 2027 and product-embedded to Aug 2028 after an 'AI Omnibus'; Claude treats the Digital Omnibus (proposed 19 Nov 2025) as a proposal to verify on EUR-Lex. Treat the deferral dates as unconfirmed.

pts: A Predetermined Change Control Plan has three parts: Description of Modifications, Modification Protocol, Impact Assessment.
If FDA authorises the PCCP, in-envelope changes can be implemented without a new marketing submission, provided only contemplated modifications are made and deployed consistently with the plan.
Aug 2025: FDA, Health Canada and MHRA issued five guiding principles — focused, risk-based, evidence-based, transparent, lifecycle-oriented.
The Claude report's assessment: the single best transferable pattern for pre-approved evolution envelopes in any regulated MAS.
Clause 10 (Improvement): 10.1 continual improvement, 10.2 nonconformity and corrective action — the continual-improvement anchor.

Annex A.6.2.2 (requirements for new or significantly enhanced systems: the change trigger), A.6.2.4 (verification and validation on change), A.6.2.6 (operation and monitoring for drift), A.6.2.8 (event logging for traceability), A.5.2 / A.5.3 (impact assessment process and documentation).
ISO/IEC 42005:2025 frames impact assessment as ongoing across updates, retraining and deployments — not a one-time check.
MANAGE 4.1: post-deployment monitoring plans including user input capture, appeal and override, decommissioning, incident response, recovery and change management.
MANAGE 4.2 (continual improvement integrated into updates), MANAGE 2.3 (respond to previously unknown risk), MANAGE 2.4 (mechanisms to supersede, disengage or deactivate — the kill switch).
MEASURE 3.1 (track emergent risks); GOVERN 1.5 (ongoing monitoring), GOVERN 1.7 (safe decommissioning). GenAI Profile adds GV-1.3 stop-build authority and continuous TEVV.
Functions: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage. Voluntary; NIST reports version 1.0 is under revision in 2026.

SR 11-7 requires effective challenge and independent validation with three elements: conceptual soundness, ongoing monitoring (does change necessitate adjustment, redevelopment or replacement), outcomes analysis; plus a model inventory and risk-based validation frequency.
Self-updating models break the assumption of discrete validated versions. Mitigation: thresholds distinguishing material change (full re-validation) from non-material (expedited).

PRA SS1/23: five principles — identification and tiering, governance, development and use with ongoing monitoring, independent validation, mitigants and reporting — explicitly extended to AI/ML and technology-agnostic.
governance.cav: Any SR 11-7 modernisation cited by industry should be confirmed on federalreserve.gov.

pts: ASI01 agent goal hijack; ASI02 tool misuse; ASI03 identity and privilege abuse; ASI04 agentic supply chain (poisoned MCP/A2A components at runtime); ASI05 unexpected code execution (self-authored code).

ASI06 memory and context poisoning (persistent corruption of memory or embeddings biasing future actions, MINJA-style); ASI08 cascading failures; ASI10 rogue agents (behavioural drift, collusion, self-replication).
Every autonomous plasticity surface must be threat-modelled against these.

Self-improvement is treated as a capability threshold: 'Autonomous AI R&D' — fully automating an entry-level remote researcher or dramatically accelerating effective scaling — requires at least ASL-3 security; v3.x references an 'AI R&D-4' threshold triggering an affirmative misalignment-risk case.
Enterprise translation: if an internal optimiser begins meaningfully accelerating your own agent R&D, escalate safeguards.

The DGM paper's own safety section — sandboxing, archive lineage, restricted web access, human oversight, and the warning that under-specified evals can amplify misalignment across generations — is the research-side counterpart.

harnesses.pl: Autoscaling policy, resource allocation, sandbox provisioning for evolution jobs.
harnesses.gt: FinOps quota and plasticity-compute budget; sandbox isolation.

harnesses.pl: Model routing and selection, decoding parameters, adapters and fine-tunes, test-time compute allocation.

hxLoop.t: Observability & FinOps emits OpenTelemetry GenAI traces from every run.
Evaluation & Assurance scores runs against suites and judges; failures are mined.
An optimiser, homed in ML & Decision Intelligence or a dedicated evolution service, proposes candidate changes.
Candidates go back through Evaluation for regression, retained-task and adversarial suites.
Governance, Oversight & AgentOps gates by risk tier (auto, human-on-the-loop, human-in-the-loop) and records the decision in the Adaptation Registry.
Security, Safety & Guardrails vetoes anything crossing a safety envelope, at any point in the loop.
Approved changes land in Memory & State, Retrieval & Context Engineering, Tool/Skill & Sandbox, Orchestration, or Model & Inference.
New traces flow back to Observability. Persistence and versioning cut across via content-addressed artifacts and registries.

patterns.d: The universal spine: optimiser proposes a candidate artifact → offline eval + regression suite → policy/safety gate + risk-tiered human approval → promote to champion. Mirrors AgentCore's shipped loop and DGM's propose → evaluate → select → archive.
All self-modification and evaluation run in isolated sandboxes with restricted network and credentials (micro-VM or Wasm for self-authored code). Never evolve in a production namespace.

Prompts, skills, tool manifests, workflow graphs and memory schemas are content-addressed, versioned, and carry provenance; an archive preserves lineage for rollback and audit (ISO A.6.2.8, EU Annex IV).
New variants run in shadow or on a traffic slice; statistical A/B confirms improvement before fleet rollout.

patterns.n: Eval gates and regression suites as immune system
patterns.d: No promotion without passing the regression suite: Law I (no safety regression), Law II (no performance regression). Beware evolving the suite itself.

patterns.n: Drift and anomaly monitoring on OTel traces
patterns.d: Standardised invoke_agent / execute_tool spans and token and cost metrics feed drift and anomaly detection: the trigger source.
TTL, quarantine of low-provenance writes, provenance scoring, poisoning detection, tenant-scoped namespaces (ASI06). Consolidation should resolve contradictions, not just append.
Cap compute and API spend per evolution run and per period; tie to Observability & FinOps. The homeostatic control.
Every promoted change is atomically reversible (NIST MANAGE 2.4); durable-execution checkpoints make rollback clean.

patterns.n: HITL vs HOTL tiers by blast radius
patterns.d: Approval intensity keyed to reversibility and impact, not agent capability: in-the-loop for irreversible or high-impact, on-the-loop for reversible medium risk, autonomous for low-risk reversible.

Tenant-scoped evolution by default; cryptographic namespace segregation for shared vector and memory stores; shared 'global' skills or prompts promoted only through a separate, stricter gate with no tenant data.

metrics: Capability
Held-out task success or pass rate
Whether accepted changes actually improve useful behaviour (Self-Harness, SWE-bench).
Retention
BWT; maximum historical score minus final score
Regressions hidden by improved average capability.
Forward transfer
FWT; samples needed on unseen tasks vs baseline
Learning-to-learn versus benchmark memorisation.
Residual plasticity
Learning-curve slope on a fresh task after N adaptation cycles
Loss of the ability to learn, not merely forgetting.
Adaptation latency
Wall-clock, episodes or interactions to recover threshold performance
Minutes versus fractions of a second matter for embodied adaptation.
Sample efficiency
Improvement per new interaction or example
Efficient plasticity versus brute-force retraining.
Safety
Unsafe-action rate, violation severity, successful attack rate
Capability gains are unacceptable if safety deteriorates (ToolEmu, AgentDojo).
Corrigibility
Intervention compliance; performance under interruption without avoidance
Whether adaptation created an incentive to resist correction.
Mutation quality
Accepted / proposed; improvement per accepted mutation
Efficiency of the self-improvement search.
Regression escape rate
Promoted changes later found to violate retained or safety tests
Verifier quality, not agent capability.
Structural complexity
New tools, modules, edges or code size per unit of gain
Unbounded harness accretion and maintainability collapse.
Diversity
Behavioural or architectural diversity of surviving lineages
Stepping stones preserved in evolutionary and QD systems.
Resource cost
Tokens, FLOPs, interactions, energy, money and time per improvement
Comparing self-evolution with ordinary engineering or retraining.
Reversibility
Successful rollback rate and state-reconstruction fidelity
Whether supposedly safe evolution can actually be undone.

gantt.n: Structural growth–pruning of tools and modules

oq: Plasticity localisation: can an agent learn which subsystem should change rather than changing everything?
Evaluator independence: how is an evolving agent prevented from adapting to, influencing, or rewriting its own judge?
Meta-stability: how is safe learning behaviour preserved when the learning rule itself is plastic?
Open-endedness versus verification: is formal assurance possible when the space of future architectures is not fixed?
Retention under semantic drift: what counts as 'the same task' after environments, tools and goals have changed?
Memory governance: how should continual agents forget deliberately for privacy, consent or legal compliance while keeping generalised knowledge?
Plasticity budgeting: can risk and uncertainty dynamically set permitted mutation magnitude, as neuromodulation gates biological learning?
Lineage and accountability: after thousands of automatic modifications, what is a reproducible system version?
Embodied plasticity: how should adaptation trade information gain against irreversible physical risk?
Alignment under self-improvement: which objectives and authority constraints must stay outside the agent's own optimisation?
